spec.prompt: A portfolio site on a Raspberry Pi 4 returns 502. Investigate the terminal and explain your reasoning as you work. All commands and readings are simulated.

steps.title: Read the error
steps.task: Reproduce the failure. Compare the proxy error log with a direct request to the app, and explain which layer failed.
hints: Try curl -I localhost, tail /var/log/nginx/error.log, and systemctl status site.
Compare the upstream address with a direct request to the port shown in the site service status.

steps.title: Fix the proxy
steps.task: Repair the upstream configuration. Validate the saved config before reloading, then verify the response.
hints: Open the editor. Saving is separate from loading the running configuration.
Try sudo nginx -t, then sudo systemctl reload nginx, then curl -I localhost.

steps.title: Fix the deploy
steps.task: Investigate the missing stylesheet. Repair access with the least permissions needed and verify it.
hints: nginx runs as www-data. Avoid making files writable by everyone.

steps.title: Free the disk
steps.task: The contact form fails. Identify what is consuming disk space, recover it safely, and test the form.
hints: An unlinked log can still consume space while a process holds it open. Truncation preserves the path.

steps.title: Check the hardware
steps.task: The site works but is slow. Investigate power and throttling, change a suitable part, and check again.
hints: Current bits and historical bits differ. measure_volts core is not the USB supply voltage.

Linux and power.description: Explains the proxy/upstream distinction and verifies a scoped configuration repair.
Explains and verifies nginx read access without granting world-write permissions.
Diagnoses disk allocation and verifies safe log recovery; distinguishes unlinking an open log from releasing its blocks.
Distinguishes current from historical throttle flags and verifies suitable power; does not treat VC4 core voltage as USB input.

Debug process.description: Explains a hypothesis, uses a targeted diagnostic, makes a scoped change and verifies the observed result. Command count alone is not ability.
